"""Product catalog used by the storefront.

get_product(product_id) -> dict    {"id": int, "name": str, "price": float, "currency": str}
update_price(product_id, price)    changes the price in the inventory service

Products read through get_product() are cached in the local Valkey server
(127.0.0.1:6379) so that every storefront process shares one cache instead of
hitting the inventory service.  Cache entries expire after 5 minutes, and
update_price() invalidates the entry so the next read gets the fresh price.
"""
import json
import urllib.request

import valkey

INVENTORY_URL = "http://127.0.0.1:8000"

VALKEY_HOST = "127.0.0.1"
VALKEY_PORT = 6379
CACHE_TTL_SECONDS = 300  # 5 minutes
KEY_PREFIX = "catalog:product:"


def _cache_key(product_id: int) -> str:
    return f"{KEY_PREFIX}{int(product_id)}"


def _get_valkey() -> valkey.Valkey:
    return valkey.Valkey(host=VALKEY_HOST, port=VALKEY_PORT, decode_responses=True)


def get_product(product_id: int) -> dict:
    product_id = int(product_id)
    client = _get_valkey()

    cached = client.get(_cache_key(product_id))
    if cached is not None:
        return json.loads(cached)

    with urllib.request.urlopen(f"{INVENTORY_URL}/products/{product_id}", timeout=10) as resp:
        product = json.load(resp)

    client.set(_cache_key(product_id), json.dumps(product), ex=CACHE_TTL_SECONDS)
    return product


def update_price(product_id: int, price: float) -> None:
    product_id = int(product_id)
    body = json.dumps({"price": price}).encode()
    req = urllib.request.Request(
        f"{INVENTORY_URL}/products/{product_id}",
        data=body,
        method="PUT",
        headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
    )
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=10) as resp:
        resp.read()

    # Invalidate the shared cache so the next get_product() (in any process)
    # returns the new price.
    _get_valkey().delete(_cache_key(product_id))
EOF

import time, sys
sys.path.insert(0, '/app')
import catalog, valkey, json

orig = catalog.get_product(1)
print("first fetch:", time.time())

t0 = time.time()
p = catalog.get_product(1)
print("second fetch took %.4fs, same data: %s" % (time.time()-t0, p == orig))

v = valkey.Valkey(host='127.0.0.1', port=6379, decode_responses=True)
print("valkey keys:", v.keys("*"))
print("ttl:", v.ttl("catalog:product:1"))

new_price = round(orig["price"] + 1.23, 2)
catalog.update_price(1, new_price)
print("after update_price, keys:", v.keys("*"))

cd /app && valkey-cli FLUSHDB >/dev/null && python3 - <<'EOF'
import subprocess, sys, time, json, urllib.request

# Process A: warm the cache
subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-c", "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'/app'); import catalog; catalog.get_product(1)"], check=True)

# Process B: must be served from Valkey (fast), even though it never fetched before
t0 = time.time()
b1 = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-c", "import sys,json; sys.path.insert(0,'/app'); import catalog; print(json.dumps(catalog.get_product(1)))"], check=True, capture_output=True, text=True)
print("process B read took %.3fs (shared cache)" % (time.time()-t0))
print("B sees:", b1.stdout.strip())

# Process A changes the price
new_price = 99.99
subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-c", f"import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'/app'); import catalog; catalog.update_price(1, {new_price})"], check=True)

# Process B: next read must return the new price
t0 = time.time()
b2 = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-c", "import sys,json; sys.path.insert(0,'/app'); import catalog; print(json.dumps(catalog.get_product(1)))"], check=True, capture_output=True, text=True)
p = json.loads(b2.stdout)
print("B after update sees price:", p["price"], "-> correct:", p["price"] == new_price, "(took %.3fs)" % (time.time()-t0))

# direct check against the service
live = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen("http://127.0.0.1:8000/products/1"))
print("service price:", live["price"])
EOF

# verify expiry actually removes the key: temporarily use a tiny TTL to exercise the mechanism
import sys, time, json, valkey
sys.path.insert(0, '/app')
import catalog

v = valkey.Valkey(host='127.0.0.1', port=6379, decode_responses=True)
v.flushdb()
catalog.get_product(1)
print("key present after get:", v.exists("catalog:product:1"))
v.expire("catalog:product:1", 2)   # same mechanism (EXPIRE), shortened for the test
time.sleep(2.5)
print("key present after 2.5s:", v.exists("catalog:product:1"))
print("real TTL set by code:", "(checked earlier: 300s)")
EOF
